components.name: ChatGPT captured interface
components.description: Single authenticated rendered DOM from an offline snapshot; no whole-site or server capture.

components.name: Offline preview
components.description: Best-effort offline preview of the captured page, not a separate live route.

components.name: Rendered application markup
components.description: Captured DOM with navigation, main content, sidebar regions and interactive elements.

components.name: Captured client-side JavaScript corpus
components.description: 144 saved JavaScript resources with diverse syntax references; execution not observed.

components.name: Captured CSS corpus
components.description: 17 saved CSS files with responsive rules, token declarations and focus styling.

components.name: Captured font-format variants
components.description: 60 available fonts in WOFF2, WOFF and TTF formats; no redistribution.

components.name: Captured image resources
components.description: 12 captured graphics in SVG, PNG and WebP formats; no redistribution.

components.name: Additional embedded HTML asset
components.description: One HTML resource among captured assets, independent of the offline preview and source DOM.

components.name: Unavailable resource attempts
components.description: Manifest lists 29 missing resources. These are capture outcomes, not proof of broken site functionality.

components.name: Browser storage references
components.description: Stored bundles contain static symbols associated with local/session storage and IndexedDB; usage unverified.

components.name: Network code indicators
components.description: Saved code contains fetch/WebSocket/EventSource-related syntax; API contracts unknown.

components.name: Media code indicators
components.description: Code-pattern evidence for WebRTC, audio and browser media APIs; no feature execution observed.

components.name: Worker and WASM indicators
components.description: Static indicators of workers, WebAssembly and dynamic imports in captured bundles.

components.name: CSS design system
components.description: Generated styles include media and container rules, design tokens and accessibility selectors.

components.name: ARIA markup census
components.description: Saved DOM exposes accessibility annotation; runtime focus and screen-reader experience were not tested.

components.name: Serialized app and route state
components.description: Captured DOM includes inline scripts and JSON data elements; state content excluded from Git.

components.name: Private evidence boundary
components.description: Original capture contains potential account-specific state, private document text, and URL parameters; all source bytes remain uncommitted.

components.name: Cross-version capture comparison
components.description: v0002 contains bundled assets unlike v0001; differing DOM counts are not proven product changes.

findings.statement: The snapshot includes a source DOM (1,666,401 bytes), a derived offline preview (515,600 bytes), a manifest and a capture notice. The preview is not another live site page.
The saved source DOM has 130 buttons, 26 anchors, 175 inline SVG elements, two nav elements, two headers, two asides, one main region and one form.
The manifest reports 234 captured resources and 29 missing resource attempts: 17 HTTP 403, ten HTTP 404 and two timeouts.
144 JavaScript resources were captured, totaling 28,066,928 source bytes. The saved code includes fetch-related syntax in 30 files; no runtime requests were observed.
Seventeen CSS resources total 2,340,628 source bytes, with hundreds of responsive, container and support-query occurrences and numerous generated style declarations.
The archive includes 60 fonts (21 WOFF2, 20 WOFF, 19 TTF), twelve images (eight SVG, three PNG, one WebP) and one embedded HTML asset.
The preview and rendered source HTML are separate files with distinct purposes; the archive contains no full server implementation or whole-site traversal.
Client storage terms appear in 26 captured JavaScript files. Static occurrence does not establish actual local storage, session storage or IndexedDB transactions.
WebSocket and EventSource terms occur in eight and two script resources respectively, while a fetch-call pattern appears in thirty. Neither endpoint targets nor network success are inferred.
WebRTC and AudioContext signatures appear in five files each, with additional media-related references. These do not prove an active media feature.
WebAssembly terms appear in three captured bundles, and dynamic-import syntax in ten. Browser workers and related code are candidate topics for further analysis.

Saved CSS contains 627 media rules, 735 supports rules, 504 container rules, 26 font-face rules, 164 keyframes, 8,135 custom property declarations, 23,269 var() references, 497 focus-visible occurrences and 168 reduced-motion references. Counts include repeated generated rules.
The captured source DOM has 152 aria-label, 160 aria-hidden, 93 aria-expanded, five aria-controls, five aria-live, and 33 tabindex attributes. Runtime accessibility remains unverified.
Nineteen script elements occur in the source DOM: sixteen inline executable scripts, two JSON data script elements and one external script reference. JSON state was not republished.
The captured source includes user/session-linked material and potentially tokenized URLs. Raw ZIP, page, manifest and asset bytes were excluded from Git.
Differences between v0001's standalone HTML and v0002's bundled snapshot establish differences in captured material, not necessarily in website releases or behavior.

Every captured website asset is enumerated in a 234-entry machine-readable inventory using capture-local ordinals. No raw URL, file path, script, stylesheet, font, image or private content is included.

Exact public asset-filename matches create 300 directed candidate references from ten captured scripts to 71 distinct JS assets, with 5,469 total string occurrences. They are neither verified imports nor evidence that referenced assets were loaded.

Seventy-two modulepreload references in the captured DOM map to saved JavaScript resources; all 18 stylesheet links resolve to the seventeen distinct saved CSS resources, with one duplicated stylesheet link.

Across 144 JavaScript files, a lexical scan finds 186 fetch-call patterns in 30 files, six WebSocket constructor patterns in six files, and 23 dynamic import patterns in ten files. These are source indicators rather than transactions or verified control paths.

The captured scripts include localStorage terms in 18 files, sessionStorage in 17, IndexedDB in four and BroadcastChannel in seven; storage keys, values and user/session data were excluded from publication.

Worker constructor patterns appear in eight files; WebAssembly member access in one, service worker references in one, and postMessage calls in 23. These do not demonstrate any worker launch or WebAssembly invocation in this session.

The seventeen CSS files contain 2,509 distinct custom-property spellings across 8,135 declarations. Width-based media rules (167), hover-related (209), reduced-motion (168), width container rules (269) and container style queries (258) describe distinct static styling mechanisms, with overlaps.

Reading the 60 captured font files' internal naming metadata yields thirteen font families and 23 family/style combinations. OpenAI Sans appears in three WOFF2 weights and the other twelve families are KaTeX-related; this does not establish which assets rendered in a given browser frame.

Captured JavaScript contains lexical references to IntersectionObserver in 30 files, ResizeObserver in 41 and MutationObserver in 32. The actual listener graph, updates and visible effects were not executed or verified.

Across saved JavaScript, 186 fetch-call patterns occur in 30 bundles. Their first arguments classify lexically into 141 identifier/call expressions, 31 other expressions and 14 literal/template starts; six WebSocket constructor patterns were found, but no actual requests were observed.

The bundles contain 987 addEventListener and 815 removeEventListener patterns, plus 65 MutationObserver, 90 ResizeObserver and 52 IntersectionObserver constructor patterns. These do not establish a DOM-to-event-handler assignment for the saved session.

Explicit browser persistence patterns include 55 localStorage reads, 34 writes and 37 removals; 40 sessionStorage reads and 46 writes; four IndexedDB open calls and ten BroadcastChannel constructors. This is static code evidence only.

One RTCPeerConnection constructor, three getUserMedia calls, one getDisplayMedia call, and one AudioContext constructor occur in saved JavaScript. These do not establish feature enablement, camera/microphone access or a successful media connection.

The CSS corpus includes 570 :has selector occurrences, 4,081 :where occurrences, 493 :focus-visible occurrences, 504 container queries, 88 display:grid declarations, 334 display:flex declarations, and 103 view-transition-related text occurrences. These are not unique rendered layout instances.

Among twelve saved image resources, one SVG is a large reusable icon sprite containing 911 symbol definitions and 1,349 path elements; three PNG files have 48×48, 180×180 and 120×120 dimensions and one WebP is 512×512. Their individual on-screen placement was not verified.

The extra HTML asset in the ZIP is a small independent document containing three script elements and one script src reference, not evidence of a separate visited site page or a running iframe workflow.

Accessible-state hooks in the DOM include 61 aria-haspopup, 13 aria-busy, five aria-live, a dialog role and a textbox role; absence of inline on* event attributes does not imply absence of JavaScript-driven events.

The saved DOM contains nonce attributes on 18 script elements and 74 link elements, a sandboxed iframe, and a referrer-policy attribute; JS uses Web Crypto syntax in seven bundles. No response-header, authorization, security or compliance audit was performed.

Compared with v0001, v0002 contains 28 more button elements, 44 more inline SVG elements and 11 more anchors. The sessions and capture methods differ, so none of these deltas is treated as a verified ChatGPT release change.

The supplied ZIP's captured HTML, 234 resources, CSS structures, media API signatures, browser state primitives, image/font metadata and candidate bundle relationships have received an evidence-bounded static analysis; runtime dependencies and browser behavior remain outside observed scope.

The supplied ZIP contains 238 entries: 234 captured resource entries and four archive-support entries. A separate manifest lists 29 unsuccessful resource attempts. This is one snapshot, not a census of the current live website.

The saved DOM nests two navigation regions inside asides and one form inside main. By closest containing landmark, its 130 buttons distribute as 70 navigation, 42 main, nine header, five aside, three form and one other. These are DOM groupings, not recovered framework component boundaries.

The 26 saved anchor destinations group into eleven site-relative, fourteen external-absolute and one fragment-only forms. The two navigation elements contain eight and 62 buttons respectively; the behavior of these controls was not observed.

The saved document has fourteen inline classic scripts, two inline module scripts, two inline JSON scripts and one external classic script. All 72 modulepreload references and the one external script match saved JS assets by source filename; declaration is not execution.

An offline JavaScript syntax-tree parse completed on all 144 saved scripts without parser diagnostics. It found 236 static import declarations and eighteen dynamic import expressions. The 236 static imports resolve to 236 distinct ordinal pairs from eight source bundles to 71 targets; eight pairs are self-ordinal references whose runtime interpretation remains unknown.

Only one captured JavaScript file includes a lexical source-map reference marker and no source-map resource is present in the ZIP. The build-tool identity and original unminified module structures cannot be asserted on this evidence.

Eighteen stylesheet link elements resolve to seventeen distinct captured CSS resources, so one target is repeated. The CSS corpus includes 33 layer at-rule text occurrences, 627 media at-rules, 504 container at-rules and no @import at-rules; no computed cascade was tested.

All 92 SVG use elements in the captured DOM reference the same captured large icon sprite and match 23 distinct symbol definitions in its 911-symbol library. This is a statically verified resource relationship, not a rendering test.

The saved accessibility structure includes 152 aria-label attributes, 93 aria-expanded attributes, 61 aria-haspopup attributes, seven status roles and a dialog and textbox role; dynamic focus and screen-reader output were not observed.

The saved markup contains eighteen scripts and 74 links with nonce attributes, plus one sandboxed iframe. HTTP response headers and runtime permissions were not captured; effective policy enforcement remains unknown.
The archive records 29 unsuccessful resource attempts: seventeen HTTP 403, ten HTTP 404 and two other failures. Their effects on live application behavior cannot be determined from the offline ZIP.

Across seventeen saved CSS files, 2,509 distinct custom properties have 8,135 declarations and 23,269 variable references. Heuristic prefix grouping finds 1,032 color and 325 typography property names, while 607 referenced names have no corresponding definition in this saved CSS corpus; the latter are not necessarily broken variables.

A bounded scan examined 573 media-condition preludes and 454 container-condition preludes from lexical totals of 627 and 504 respectively. Overlapping categories include 159 width-media, 178 hover-media, 60 pointer-media, 168 reduced-motion-media and 258 container style-query matches. These do not prove actual responsive layout states.

The CSS corpus includes 164 keyframe-rule text occurrences, 438 transition declarations, 287 animation declarations, 270 duration declarations and 168 reduced-motion media preludes across ten stylesheets. These are available motion facilities, not observed animations or reduced-motion outcomes.

An offline syntax-tree pass over 144 JavaScript resources traversed 9,273,632 AST nodes, including 120,699 function-like nodes. Fixed API-signature categories overlap across 48 React-like, 54 network, 46 browser-state, 89 event/observer, seven media and seventeen worker-related bundles. These groups are code-study candidates, not verified module ownership.

Saved HTML declares 72 captured modulepreloads; JavaScript contains 236 static imports and eighteen dynamic import expressions. A rendered document, initialization scripts and React-like source hooks are also present. The ZIP cannot show the executed load/hydration sequence.

AST-level callsites include 997 event-listener registrations, 822 removals, 144 animation-frame calls and 67, 90 and 57 mutation, resize and intersection observer constructors. It also contains 133 useState and 134 useEffect calls by fixed-name syntax; no individual DOM control-to-handler mapping was observed.

Generic storage method signatures include 118 getItem, 102 setItem and 78 removeItem calls; message-related constructs include eleven BroadcastChannel, 25 MessageChannel, eight Worker and 77 postMessage patterns. Twelve lexical function scopes combine worker/messaging and channel signatures. Stored values and actual messages were not observed.

The syntax trees contain 178 fetch calls, 244 AbortController, sixteen getReader, 33 TextDecoder, six WebSocket and three peer-connection call/constructor signatures. Five lexical function scopes contain both fetch and streaming signatures, and six contain fetch and abort signatures. No actual API transaction or retry policy is established.

The saved DOM has 2,183 elements, 1,688 with classes and 744 distinct class names. A plain unescaped CSS class-selector scan finds 3,776 distinct selector class names in 16,983 rules; 359 names overlap the DOM and 1,666 class-bearing DOM elements have one or more overlapping labels. These are vocabulary matches, not verified computed selectors or component ownership.

Font metadata from sixty files separates 57 mathematical typesetting assets and three interface sans faces across 21 WOFF2, twenty WOFF and nineteen TTF containers. Font weight metadata includes forty weight-400, eighteen weight-700, one weight-500 and one weight-600 files. Actual glyph usage is unknown.

Static accessibility indicators include 152 aria-label, 93 aria-expanded, 61 aria-haspopup attributes, a dialog and textbox role, CSS focus-visible selectors and reduced-motion conditions. Their presence does not demonstrate actual keyboard navigation or assistive-technology announcements.

Captured resources comprise 28,066,928 script bytes, 2,341,104 stylesheet bytes, 1,169,636 font bytes, 725,265 image bytes and 13,236 supplemental-document bytes. The five largest scripts comprise 36.38% of captured JavaScript bytes and the ten largest comprise 57.71%; actual download, cache and render timing were not measured.

Semantic DOM landmarks and selector overlap cannot identify original framework components, props or output owners. This saved ZIP lacks executable event ownership traces and captured source maps; precise component and route-loader linkage remains unsupported.

The project-authored architectural story connects observed markup, preload declarations, parsed import syntax, CSS vocabulary and browser API callsite classes. The flow is explicitly explanatory and conditional, not a browser execution trace.
The Specimen Atlas presents original evidence-backed HTML, CSS, JavaScript, component, logic, flow, state, asset and research chapters, plus sanitized interactive graphs and queue views.

The final source-scope audit distinguishes statically investigable mechanisms from component ownership, live interactions, authentication, media transfers, dynamic accessibility, measured performance and product release comparisons that the ZIP cannot establish.

The captured source contains identifiable public runtime/style signatures for React, React Router, Tailwind CSS, Radix UI, ProseMirror and KaTeX. Additional library signatures for Floating UI, TanStack Query, React Markdown/micromark, motion and highlighting have lower certainty. None of these observations establishes exact dependency versions or executed features; the separately published technology inventory records specific evidence and qualifications.

The saved document has a large aside containing two navigation regions, one main landmark with a header and form, and one role=dialog region. The sidebar contains 74 descendant buttons, the two nav subtrees 8 and 62, main 51, the composer form three buttons and four file inputs, and the dialog four buttons. These descendant counts overlap and identify captured DOM structure, not an exact pixel layout or original framework component tree.

A source-level AST scan of 144 captured JavaScript resources found generic conversation-identity-like identifiers in 63 resources, message-identity-like identifiers in 43, and parent-reference-like identifiers in sixteen. These are program token categories, not recovered API data fields.

Of 113,643 parsed object literals, 391 contain conversation and message-like property categories, one contains message and parent categories, and two contain parent and graph-edge categories. Static co-location cannot verify the meaning of message ancestry or the running data model.

Across 120,699 function-like nodes, eighteen scopes contain message and parent categories, nineteen parent and graph-edge categories, seven branch and message categories, and five network and streaming categories. These are static syntactic associations, not executed chat behavior.

The saved document has one contenteditable textbox within the main form and four file inputs. Four buttons in the main region carry edit-related label indicators, four carry regeneration indicators, eight carry copy indicators, and seventeen new-chat indicators occur across navigation and headers. These are matched attribute labels, not observed action outcomes or distinct functional controls.

Public documentation establishes that ChatGPT can export conversation JSON. Independent export-parser documentation describes a legacy/tree-shaped structure with mapping, parent, children and current_node fields, enabling branch and selected-path reconstruction in exported data. This does not verify that the v0002 browser client, a current private endpoint, or the backend uses the same representation.

The captured client defines selected-ancestry traversal through a node mapping and exposes a branching operation that supplies a conversation and message identity. These are source-level client implementations, not verified backend storage.

Six captured generation entrypoints directly delegate to a shared generation dispatcher; that dispatcher invokes a completion-stream client and wires decoded events, completion, recoverable errors and resumption callbacks. These are source call relationships, not observed network outcomes.

Decoded message updates enter a captured event processor and reach a client graph mutator. The mutator inserts or updates nodes, maintains parent/child relationships, can rotate a descendant and returns new-node/rotation flags; the caller conditionally preserves or advances the selected node.

The captured conversation state writer commits the revised mapping and selected node, derives separate automation and page-reference collections from messages on the selected ancestry path, and maintains a user-message ancestry list. The automation/page collections are not the visible chat transcript; actual message-rendering subscribers remain untraced.

The captured completion transport supports distinct start/resume pathways, topic-stream and streaming-request alternatives, local/request cancellation, recovery callbacks and WebSocket stream-item duplicate/missing-parent checks. Actual server delivery and recovery success remain unobserved.

The captured client defines separate full selected-message ancestry and recent-turn ancestry selectors from mapping/current_node. A React conversation control subscribes to the recent-turn selector to derive answer-now eligibility; other selectors consume user-message ancestry and feature-specific automation references. The automation/page-reference collections are not the visible chat transcript, and no live rendering was observed.

A captured React conversation control subscribes to recent-turn messages and renders inline and Escape-dialog buttons with bound click handlers. One guarded path requests answer-now steering; another requests stopping an active response and, upon permitted completion, regeneration with reasoning skipped. Error handling resets pending state. These are inspected client paths, not observed interactions.

The captured client has a source-backed transcript rendering pipeline: conversation mapping/current selection drive derived turn entries with typed items; a turn-preparation stage may add a pending user item and suppress the first user item for particular presentation modes; the conversation page passes prepared turns to an exported turn configurator; an item renderer branches by message/tool/media kind and attaches role, source-message and test identifiers to DOM wrappers. Exact runtime visibility and dynamic-import behavior remain unverified.

Static inspection of the saved transcript renderer establishes distinct presentation rules for pending-message insertion/deduplication, loading indicators, first-user-item hiding, latest-turn error/attachment placement, an alternate selected-message derivation, simplified sidebar/moderation item treatment, reasoning/tool/streaming grouping and DOM role/telemetry wrappers. These are source-level conditional display paths, not evidence of server data mutation or runtime execution.

The captured typed conversation-turn renderer forwards client edit, regeneration and fork callbacks to message or turn action components. User-message editing is gated by item type, eligible identity and attachment/targeted-reply restrictions; regeneration is suppressed for some read-only and special-turn states; fork handling is passed to the action row. These are static callback and presentation conditions, not observed user actions or server outcomes.

The saved client renders previous/next response-version controls from an ordered variant list and selected index. Choosing a variant calls an imported selection helper that validates a mapped selected descendant, updates the current node optimistically, constructs a persistence request, and restores the prior selection after failure while clearing busy state. These are captured client operations; no live click, server acknowledgement or durable outcome is verified.

The captured response-version selector derives alternatives from the conversation mapping: it walks from the selected response toward a qualifying prompt ancestor, enumerates that prompt's child branches, filters candidate descendants for selectable variants, and computes an active variant index against the current selected ancestry path. The filtered selectable list can differ from the raw prompt-child count. This is client-side source behavior, not proof of backend persistence.

limitations: Only a single captured authenticated browser state and its fetched assets are available; no whole-site crawl or backend source is included.
Some bundled code may be inactive, feature-flagged, or unrelated to this user-visible session. Pattern matches do not establish functionality.
Twenty-nine resources were not captured because of HTTP responses or timeouts.
No live network waterfall, actual event execution, browser performance traces, or response-header security audit was performed.
The offline preview is a derivative, not an independent site page.
Private session state and tokenized links in the source are excluded from Git.
v0001 and v0002 differ in capture depth and DOM state; numeric differences are not verified product changes.
The final static review cannot attribute minified event listeners to individual rendered controls or prove focus behavior without runtime or sourcemap evidence.
The ZIP contains source patterns for media, network, security and client storage; captured code is not evidence that any feature was enabled, called successfully, or executed on this page.
Rendered-state and archive-depth differences between v0001 and v0002 cannot be interpreted as verified product changes.
Offline research identifies structural mechanisms but not actual runtime component, storage, network, permission or accessibility behavior.
Like-for-like site release comparison and live performance timing cannot be derived from unmatched capture states.
